name: splice-equivalence-tests-are-code-only
body:
source: the brief, "the splice-equivalence tests are code-only ... the merge e2e always adds code, so it never isolates the spec-only case".

Inconsistency: verified [autonomous] — `rust.splice_e2e.fixture_graph` (tests/splice_e2e.rs:21) builds only Module/File/Struct/Function/UnresolvedTarget with code rels; `rust.splice_e2e.e2e.delta_application_matches_a_full_rebuild` compares `code_snapshot` only; `rust.splice_e2e.e2e.spliced_and_full_rebuild_agree_on_every_table_count` compares every `show_tables()` count, but on the same code-only fixture the authored tables are empty on both sides, so the authored-table equality is vacuous; `rust.project_cmd_e2e.e2e.merge_round_trip_start_mutate_verify_merge_rebuild` writes Widget and rescans the branch (`start_scan_locked(&wt)`) before merging, advancing the shared store so the seed guard mismatches.

Resolution: `requirements.requirement.spec-only-splice-equivalence-tests` requires a spec-only merge e2e and a spec-only delta test. Their test FQNs do not exist yet, so they are declared as planned Implementation nodes with `creates` tasks at plan time — never invented here. [autonomous]
